# Section documentation for [STACK-Maxima](../../index.md) /linearalgebra/predicates

Predicates for matrix shape and algebraic properties, available in core STACK.

Use [`col_vecp`](#col_vecp), [`row_vecp`](#row_vecp) and [`vectorp`](#vectorp) to distinguish column and row matrices;
use [`squarep`](#squarep), [`diagp`](#diagp), [`triup`](#triup) and [`trilp`](#trilp) to check their structure. A diagonal
matrix may be rectangular, and a triangular matrix need not be invertible or
in row echelon form.

Use [`REFp`](#REFp) for row echelon form, [`symp`](#symp) for symmetry, [`invertiblep`](#invertiblep) for
invertibility, and [`diagonalizablep`](#diagonalizablep) for diagonalizability. The orthogonality
predicates test columns using the standard inner product (the dot product for
real vectors, conjugated in the second slot for complex vectors) or a supplied
scalar product.

Most predicates require a Maxima matrix. [`orthogonal_columnsp`](#orthogonal_columnsp) and
[`orthonormal_columnsp`](#orthonormal_columnsp) also accept lists of column vectors through
`cols_to_matrix`. Consult each function for its accepted inputs and optional
arguments. Simplification and Maxima's ability to recognise zero expressions
can affect the result; add explicit size or entry constraints when needed.


---


## REFp(M,[normalize_pivots])<a id='REFp'></a>

Predicate to determine whether a matrix is in row echelon form
i.e. Is every zero-row below all non-zero rows and does the pivot in each row appear to the right of the previous pivot?
Optionally checks whether each pivot is equal to 1
Non-matrix input returns `false`. The zero matrix and matrices with no
entries satisfy these conditions. Pivots are identified using `is`; simplify
entries first if algebraically zero expressions should be recognised.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | An mxn matrix |
| normalize_pivots | boolean | Optional: If true is given here, then pivots are required to be equal to 1 |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | Is this matrix in row echelon form? |


---


## col_vecp(ex)<a id='col_vecp'></a>

Return `true` when the argument is a Maxima matrix with exactly one column.
A 1-by-1 matrix satisfies both [`col_vecp`](#col_vecp) and [`row_vecp`](#row_vecp).

For example, `col_vecp(matrix([a],[b]))` is `true`, but
`col_vecp(matrix([a,b]))` and `col_vecp(c(a,b))` are `false`.
Use `vec_convert` first when accepting the inert `c`/`r` notation.
Lists, scalars and `matrix()` return `false`.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| ex | expression | the object whose shape is checked. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | whether the object is a matrix with exactly one column. |


---


## diagonalizablep(M)<a id='diagonalizablep'></a>

Is a given object a diagonalizable matrix?
i.e. Is there an invertible matrix P and diagonal matrix D such that P^^-1 . M . P = D?

This uses Maxima's `jordan` and `dispJordan` functions and inherits their
computational limits. Non-square and non-matrix inputs return `false`.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | a matrix |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | Is M a diagonalizable matrix? |


---


## diagp(M)<a id='diagp'></a>

Return `true` when the argument is a matrix whose off-diagonal entries
are recognised as zero by `is`. The matrix need not be square; use [`squarep`](#squarep)
as well if the task requires a square diagonal matrix. Diagonal entries
may be zero or symbolic.
Rectangular diagonal matrices occur as the Sigma factor in a singular value
decomposition (SVD).

For example, `diagp(matrix([a,0,0],[0,b,0]))` is `true`, but
`diagp(matrix([1,x],[0,1]))` is `false` for an unconstrained symbol `x`.
Non-matrix arguments return `false`. Empty matrices have no off-diagonal
entries to reject, so `matrix()`, `matrix([])` and `matrix([],[])` return `true`.

The simplification mode matters. With `simp:false`, the off-diagonal
entry `1-1` in `matrix([1,0],[1-1,1])` is not simplified and this predicate
returns `false`; with `simp:true` it returns `true`. Simplify the matrix
explicitly first if algebraically zero expressions should be accepted.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | expression | the object whose off-diagonal entries are checked. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | whether every off-diagonal entry is recognised as zero. |


---


## invertiblep(M)<a id='invertiblep'></a>

Is a given object an invertible matrix?
i.e. Is there a matrix M^^-1 such that M^^-1 . M = M . M^^-1 = I?
A square matrix is accepted when Maxima recognises its simplified
determinant as nonzero. Non-square and non-matrix inputs return `false`.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | a matrix |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | Is M an invertible matrix? |


---


## orth_matrixp(M)<a id='orth_matrixp'></a>

Is a given object an orthogonal matrix (real entries) or a unitary matrix (complex entries)?
i.e. Is M^* . M = M . M^* = I, where M^* is the conjugate transpose (M^T for a real M)?
Requires a square Maxima matrix and uses the standard inner product.
Unlike [`orthonormal_columnsp`](#orthonormal_columnsp), this function has no scalar-product argument.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | a matrix |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | Is M an orthogonal matrix? |


---


## orthogonal_columnsp(L,[sp])<a id='orthogonal_columnsp'></a>

Does the given matrix/list have orthogonal columns with respect to scalar product sp?
i.e. for any two distinct columns v1 and v2, is sp(v1, v2) = 0?
Returns false in case of malformed input.
In case no scalar product is provided, the standard inner product is used: the dot product
for real vectors, and u^T.conjugate(v) for complex vectors (linear in the first slot).



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| L | matrix | A mxn matrix or list of column vectors, see cols_to_matrix |
| sp | function or matrix | (Optional) A scalar product or a positive definite (real symmetric, or Hermitian) matrix S representing a scalar product sp(u, v) := u^T.S.conjugate(v) |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | Does L have orthogonal columns with respect to sp? |


---


## orthonormal_columnsp(L,[sp])<a id='orthonormal_columnsp'></a>

Does the given matrix/list have orthonormal columns with respect to scalar product sp?
i.e. for columns v_i and v_j, is sp(v_i, v_i) = 1 and sp(v_i, v_j) = 0 for i # j?
Returns false in case of malformed input.
In case no scalar product is provided, the standard inner product is used: the dot product
for real vectors, and u^T.conjugate(v) for complex vectors (linear in the first slot).



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| L | matrix | A mxn matrix or list of column vectors, see cols_to_matrix |
| sp | function or matrix | (Optional) A scalar product or a positive definite (real symmetric, or Hermitian) matrix S representing a scalar product sp(u, v) := u^T.S.conjugate(v) |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | Does L have orthonormal columns with respect to sp? |


---


## row_vecp(ex)<a id='row_vecp'></a>

Return `true` when the argument is a Maxima matrix with exactly one row.
A 1-by-1 matrix satisfies both [`row_vecp`](#row_vecp) and [`col_vecp`](#col_vecp).

For example, `row_vecp(matrix([a,b]))` is `true`, but
`row_vecp(matrix([a],[b]))` and `row_vecp(r(a,b))` are `false`.
Use `vec_convert` first when accepting the inert `c`/`r` notation.
Lists, scalars and `matrix()` return `false`.

This is a shape check: `matrix([])` has one row and no columns, so it
returns `true`. Check the number of columns separately if entries are required.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| ex | expression | the object whose shape is checked. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | whether the object is a matrix with exactly one row. |


---


## squarep(M)<a id='squarep'></a>

Return `true` when the argument is a matrix with equal row and column counts.
The entries need not be numeric, and a square matrix need not be invertible.

For example, `squarep(matrix([a,b],[c,d]))` is `true`, while
`squarep(matrix([a],[b]))` and `squarep([a,b])` are `false`.
The empty 0-by-0 matrix `matrix()` returns `true`; `matrix([])` returns
`false`. Check the size separately if a nonempty square matrix is required.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | expression | the object whose shape is checked. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | whether the object is a square matrix. |


---


## symp(M)<a id='symp'></a>

Is a given object a symmetric matrix?
i.e. Is M = M^T?
This uses transpose without complex conjugation, so it tests symmetry,
not the Hermitian property. Non-square and non-matrix inputs return `false`.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | matrix | a matrix |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | Is M a symmetric matrix? |


---


## trilp(M)<a id='trilp'></a>

Return `true` when every entry above the main diagonal of a Maxima matrix
is recognised as zero by `is`. The matrix may be rectangular; use [`squarep`](#squarep)
as well if a square lower triangular matrix is required.

For example, `trilp(matrix([a,0],[b,c],[d,e]))` is `true`.
Diagonal entries may be zero or symbolic, so this does not test invertibility
or row echelon form. Use [`triup`](#triup) to check the other triangular part.

Non-matrix arguments, including lists and inert `c`/`r` expressions, return
`false`. With no entries to reject, `matrix()`, `matrix([])` and
`matrix([],[])` return `true`.

The simplification mode matters: `trilp(matrix([1,1-1],[0,1]))` returns `false`
with `simp:false` and `true` with `simp:true`. Simplify the matrix first if
algebraically zero expressions should be accepted.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | expression | the object whose triangular structure is checked. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | whether every entry above the diagonal is recognised as zero. |


---


## triup(M)<a id='triup'></a>

Return `true` when every entry below the main diagonal of a Maxima matrix
is recognised as zero by `is`. The matrix may be rectangular; use [`squarep`](#squarep)
as well if a square upper triangular matrix is required.

For example, `triup(matrix([a,b,c],[0,d,e]))` is `true`.
Diagonal entries may be zero or symbolic, so this does not test invertibility
or row echelon form. Use [`trilp`](#trilp) to check the other triangular part.

Non-matrix arguments, including lists and inert `c`/`r` expressions, return
`false`. With no entries to reject, `matrix()`, `matrix([])` and
`matrix([],[])` return `true`.

The simplification mode matters: `triup(matrix([1,0],[1-1,1]))` returns `false`
with `simp:false` and `true` with `simp:true`. Simplify the matrix first if
algebraically zero expressions should be accepted.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| M | expression | the object whose triangular structure is checked. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | whether every entry below the diagonal is recognised as zero. |


---


## vectorp(ex)<a id='vectorp'></a>

Return `true` for a matrix accepted by either [`col_vecp`](#col_vecp) or [`row_vecp`](#row_vecp).
This includes 1-by-1 matrices. It does not accept lists or inert `c`/`r`
expressions; apply `vec_convert` first if the `c`/`r` forms are permitted.

For example, `vectorp(matrix([a],[b]))` and `vectorp(matrix([a,b]))`
are `true`, while `vectorp(matrix([a,b],[c,d]))` is `false`.
As with [`row_vecp`](#row_vecp), the one-row empty matrix `matrix([])` is accepted;
`matrix()` is not. This predicate does not check entries or non-emptiness.



| Argument name | type | description |
| ------------- | ---- | ----------- |
| ex | expression | the object whose shape is checked. |




| Return type | description |
| ----------- | ------------|
| boolean | whether the object is a row or column matrix. |
